-PART 1 WORKPLACES

0.

FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard ( Part 1 )!was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 3 August 1987, after the draft finalized by the Cement and Civil Concrete Sectional Committee had been approved by the Engineering Division Council.
0.2 In recent years there has been a growing awareness that exposure to asbestos dust can have harmful effects on the health of workers. Accordingly, a number of standards giving technical guidance on how the risk of exposure to asbestos dust can be prevented, controlled or minimized have been taken up for formulation. It has also been felt necessary that some pictorial warning signs and precautionary notices shall be used at workplaces involving asbestos and asbestos products, packages containing asbestos and asbestos products, and also on the asbestos products, in order to caution the workers and users about the Keeping this in view, this stan1'ar.d potential health hazards of asbestos. regarding pictorial warning signs and precautionary notices has been formulated in two parts as follows: a) Recommendations for pictorial warning signs and precautionary notices for asbestos and products containing asbestos: Part 1 Workplaces; and b) Recommendations for pictorial warning signs and precautionary notices for asbestos and products containing asbestos: Part 2 Asbestos and its products. 0.3 In the formulation of this standard due weightage has been given to international co-ordination among the standards and practices prevailing in different countries in addition to relating it to the practices in the field in this country. 3

1987

1.1 This standard ( Part 1 ) deals with pictorial warning signs precautionary notices to be used at workplaces involving asbestos products containing asbestos.
2. OBJECT

of asbestos and

those engaged in handling so as to enable them to take the risk from exposure to

3.1 Workplaces with a potential to release airborne asbestos dust shall be clearly indicated as asbestos dust exposure area through the use of well-displayed pictorial warning signs and notices. The purpose of these warning signs/notices is to ensure that asbestos is not worked upon without appropriate precautions and to restrict the entry to authorized persons only. 3.2 Where airborne asbestos dust concentration is above the action level but below the permissible exposure limit ( see IS : 11451-1986" ), pictorial warning sign and notice given in Fig. 1 shall be used. 3.3 Where airborne asbestos dust concentration exceeds the permissible limit, pictorial warning sign and notice given in Fig. 2 shall exposure be used. 3.4 Size - The dimensions of the pictorial warning sign shall be not less than 300 x 430 mm for Fig. 1 and 300 x 600 mm for Fig. 2.
